To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimality of randomized tests for distributed detection is not a general property.
the optimal test does NOT randomize, and that this is true for any fusion rule.
the optimal fusion test in a distributed detection system does not randomize when the raw data are independent and do not have any point-masses of the likelihood ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of distributed detection of a target in a cluttered environment.
the problem of optimal decentralized detection of a parameter in a network of sensor nodes, each of which is connected to a fusion center by a noisy channel.
the development of a general framework for the design of decentralized detection systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal test does never randomize.
the optimal test for decentralized detection is nonrandomized if the likelihood ratios are continuous and do not contain point-masses of probabilities.
the optimal fusion rule for decentralized detection systems is not randomized, and the quantizer mappings are not necessarily monotone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the suboptimality of the randomized tests in distributed detection systems is not due to the fact that the observations are quantized.
, if the likelihood ratios are continuous random variables, and the likelihood ratio test is optimal for the raw observations, then it is also optimal for the quantized observations.

, in a decentralized detection system, it is not optimal for the local detectors to randomize, i.e., to use randomized decision rules, and the optimal test is a deterministic function of the likelihood ratios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given quantization scheme, there is no advantage to randomization in the design of a test for a decentralized detection problem.
the design search for optimal decentralized detection systems can be simplified by considering only deterministic tests.
the suboptimality of the randomized test in distributed and quantised detection systems is a consequence of the fact that the raw observations are continuous random variables.
